sources.entry: Git Interactive Rebase Tool - Full feature terminal based sequence editor for interactive rebase.

summary.one_liner: A cross-platform, full-featured terminal sequence editor for Git interactive rebase, written in Rust.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a terminal-based editor that Git uses as the sequence editor during interactive rebase (Git 1.7.8+). It lets you set each commit's action to pick, squash, fixup, edit, reword or drop, and reorder commits with a key press. Visual mode allows changing actions and moving multiple lines at once. You can view commit details and full diffs, edit exec commands, toggle break actions, and shell out to an external editor. An optional setting injects exec lines after modified commits, for example to amend messages or run tests on changed commits. Built-in help is available with the ? key.
use_cases: Reorder or squash commits during git rebase -i
Reword commit messages in a terminal
Clean up commit history before merging
Run tests on only modified commits during a rebase
Use a visual, keyboard-driven todo list editor for git
how_to_run: git rebase -i <base> (uses the tool as the sequence editor)
notable: Works as a drop-in git sequence.editor with a single git config line
Visual mode for changing actions and reordering multiple lines at once
Optional postModifiedLineExecCommand hook that injects exec lines after changed commits
Packaging for Debian and RPM, with reproducible build support via SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
caveats: Windows before version 10 has rendering issues with saturated dark colors
Git Bash needs winpty, and Windows Console and Git Bash get only minimal support
Windows Console in legacy mode is not supported and Cygwin is not officially supported
Other platforms are not officially supported
